implementation_notes: Swift's concurrency runtime absorbs the pill into the stream API: an AsyncStream producer keeps calling continuation.yield(job) and ends the stream with continuation.finish(), which makes the iterator produce nil and terminates every for await loop after the buffered elements; onTermination is where the consumer cleans up. That replaces the hand-rolled sentinel for callback or delegate sources adapted to async sequences, and one finish() serves every iterator of that stream. For pre-async DispatchQueue/OperationQueue workers there is no close primitive, so a sentinel element - or OperationQueue.cancelAllOperations()/DispatchWorkItem.cancel() for hard stops - is still needed.
pitfalls: finish() is not a cancellation: buffered elements are still delivered first, and yielding after finish() is dropped - the drain is the point.
Cancelling the consuming Task ends for await without draining the buffer (and throws CancellationError in throwing variants); handle task cancellation separately from the pill.
onTermination runs on finish, cancellation and deinit, so cleanup must be idempotent and must not assume an orderly drain.
The stream's buffering policy still applies: with .bufferingNewest(n) older jobs may already have been dropped before finish() terminates the loop.
